title: Abelian cartesian local heart and exact evaluations
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D and coefficient datum c [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and a locally finite-type k0-scheme T. Let Hloc(T) be the literal category of cartesian local heart objects on separated finite-type opens [def-dl-a1-locally-constructible-adic-heart]. Each component category is the common-stage standard heart over k0 [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres, def-weil-constructible-heart]. There are Abelian structures on Hloc(T) and all these component categories [def-sp-abelian], for which every literal evaluation functor is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. This assertion constructs only the algebraic category and exact evaluation; it asserts no cover detection or defect-vanishing equivalence.

source.place: §6.8, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; local cartesian heart defects on finite-type affine opens (returned proof Step 12). Stacks Tag 04TQ, sites-lemma-glue-maps.

proof.text: For each basis open $V$, use the bounded common-stage standard t-structure over $k_0$ supplied by [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. Its heart $\mathcal H_V$ is abelian by [prop-weil-heart-abelian]. For $U\subseteq V$ in the basis, apply [lem-per-adic-stratified-pullback-texact] with base field $k_0$: the actual completed restriction $r_{UV}$ is additive and exact on hearts. Both schemes are separated finite type over this field and $\ell$ is invertible there. Use the composition comparisons and cocycle specified in [def-dl-a1-locally-constructible-adic-heart]. These are the given common-stage functors; no coefficient field is chosen on $T$.

Addition and negation of compatible arrow families preserve their compatibility equations, since all $r_{UV}$ are additive. Thus the Hom sets are abelian groups and composition is bilinear componentwise. The family of zero objects, with the unique restriction comparisons, is a zero object. For $A,B$, form $(A\oplus B)_V=A_V\oplus B_V$; use the additive restriction comparisons and the direct sums of their given gluing maps. Their cocycle and the injection/projection identities are checked in each component, so this gives binary biproducts. These constructions use exactly the compatible-family category of [def-dl-a1-locally-constructible-adic-heart].

source.place: Agent argument on compatible families, following Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: For $f:A\to B$, set $N_V=\ker f_V$, with inclusion $i_V:N_V\to A_V$. Exactness and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a) identify $r_{UV}N_V$ with $\ker(r_{UV}f_V)$. The square for $f$ conjugates this kernel to $N_U$; define $\rho^N_{UV}$ to be its unique isomorphism satisfying $i_U\rho^N_{UV}=\rho^A_{UV}r_{UV}i_V$. On a triple of nested opens the two induced arrows into $N_U$ agree after $i_U$, by the cocycle for $A$ and naturality of the composition comparison. Since $i_U$ is monic they agree. Identities follow by the same cancellation. Hence $N$ is cartesian and $i:N\to A$ is compatible. Given a compatible $h:D\to A$ with $fh=0$, let $t_V:D_V\to N_V$ be its unique kernel lift. The two compatibility composites for $t$ agree after $i_U$, both equalling the compatibility composite for $h$; cancellation makes $t$ compatible. Componentwise uniqueness proves the global kernel universal property.

source.place: Agent kernel construction using the exact completed restrictions of Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: Set $Q_V=\operatorname{coker}f_V$, with projection $p_V:B_V\to Q_V$. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a), $r_{UV}p_V$ is a cokernel of $r_{UV}f_V$. Conjugating by the given comparisons defines a unique isomorphism $\rho^Q_{UV}$ with $\rho^Q_{UV}r_{UV}p_V=p_U\rho^B_{UV}$. On a triple the cocycle for $B$ makes the two arrows to $Q_U$ agree after the epimorphism obtained by restricting $p_V$ twice, so they agree; this also gives identity normalization. For $h:B\to D$ with $hf=0$, its unique component factorizations $t_V:Q_V\to D_V$ are compatible: precompose the proposed compatibility equation with the epimorphism $r_{UV}p_V$ and use that for $h$. Thus $p:B\to Q$ is a global cokernel, with its universal property. In particular both kernels and cokernels evaluate to the corresponding component constructions.

source.place: Agent cokernel construction using the exact completed restrictions of Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: Let $f:A\to B$ be monic in the compatible-family category. Its kernel inclusion $i:N\to A$ has $fi=0$, whence $i=0$ by monicity; since $i$ is itself monic, $\mathrm{id}_N=0$. Thus every $\ker f_V=N_V$ is zero, so $f_V$ is monic in the abelian heart $\mathcal H_V$. There it is a kernel of its cokernel $p_V$. For any compatible $h:D\to B$ with $ph=0$, factor $h_V$ uniquely through $f_V$. The factors are compatible because composing their proposed compatibility equation with the monomorphism $f_U$ gives that of $h$. They give the unique factorization through $f$. Hence every global monomorphism is a kernel of its cokernel.

source.place: Agent verification of the normal-monomorphism axiom of an abelian category

proof.text: Let $f:A\to B$ be epic. For its cokernel $p:B\to Q$, $pf=0$ implies $p=0$; since $p$ is epic, $\mathrm{id}_Q=0$. Every component cokernel is therefore zero, so $f_V$ is epic in $\mathcal H_V$ and is a cokernel of its kernel $i_V$. Given compatible $h:A\to D$ with $hi=0$, its unique factorizations through $f_V$ are compatible: precompose the compatibility equation with the epimorphism $r_{UV}f_V$ and use that for $h$. Uniqueness holds componentwise. Thus every epimorphism is a cokernel of its kernel. Together with Steps 2--4 this proves all the axioms of [def-sp-abelian].

source.place: Agent verification of the normal-epimorphism axiom and abelian-category definition

proof.text: Evaluation preserves component biproducts, kernels and cokernels by the explicit universal properties in Steps 2--4. Thus it is additive; the usual finite-product-and-kernel and finite-coproduct-and-cokernel descriptions in an abelian category give preservation of finite limits and finite colimits.

mathlib_searches.query: A category of cartesian families of abelian categories is abelian and evaluation preserves finite limits and colimits
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits: Abelian.hasFiniteLimits and evaluation preservation of limits/colimits in ordinary functor categories and homological complexes. These do not construct the specified varying cartesian heart or establish open-cover detection.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No match: the local category is not an ordinary functor category in a fixed target.

mathlib_searches.query: The category of cartesian families in abelian categories with exact restriction functors is abelian, and evaluation is exact
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits: condensed AB4/AB4Star instances, Grothendieck AB4, AddCommGrp AB4Star, and Functor.exact_tfae. None constructs the literal cartesian adic heart.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No match. Exact-functor comparison results are useful after the cartesian abelian construction.

mathlib_searches.results: 12 hits including IsZero, IsZero.hasZeroObject, IsZero.iso and isZero_zero. These concern generic zero objects, not cartesian adic families. The separate query kernelComparison, IsIso returned no hits.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No match for either cartesian abelian construction or cover detection.
